title: Configure many Monitors with optional sponsoring sections
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a publication editor, I want several independently configured Monitors, so that source discovery follows publication needs without a single owning desk.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Configure many Monitors with optional sponsoring sections
  Scenario: Configure independent monitors
    Given one publication has multiple curated sections
    When I configure several Monitors with source type, source/query scope and collection bounds
    Then each has a stable identity and independently visible configuration and run status
    And a Monitor may optionally record a sponsoring section or newsdesk
    And sponsorship is retained as provenance rather than exclusive Reference ownership
  Scenario: Configure another publication
    Given a publication with a different subject and doctrine
    When I configure its Monitors
    Then no Threat Intelligence-specific fields or assumptions are required
```

Define configuration placement and publication authorization against current steering/section hierarchy during implementation design. No duplication of section curation or embedded provider secrets.

Latest priority and initial consumers: inbound Monitoring is Ryan's highest near-term value, independent of Markus for everything, outbound RSS/Atom and headless delivery. Initial consumers are the academic Papyrus publication, Threat Intelligence AND Anth.us, configured through the same publication-agnostic Papyrus capability rather than special implementations. Morning relevant discoveries must reach the actual configured Cyclotron classifiers with attributable classification evidence; a manual research list alone is not completion. No automatic human labels. No blocking dependency on the Markus initiative, outgoing feeds, authored-page migration or email-monitor implementation is introduced.

First small vertical slice: validate and configure a later expansion to 3–5 real sources across those consumers, prioritizing Hacker News, arXiv AI papers, the current Hugging Face paper offering, security/privacy publications and CVE/advisory sources. Final source/publication bindings are verified, not inferred. Cadence is configurable around 15 minutes where source limits and update frequency permit, with checkpoints, deduplication, new/updated-item handling, provenance and visible retryable failures. The desired “tonight or tomorrow” urgency expresses value, not permission to deploy or start coding.

Source validation evidence from this planning pass: https://huggingface.co/papers currently identifies Daily Papers (daily/weekly/monthly views) and offers email subscription; no official RSS feed, stable API contract or Papers With Code successor status was established. Validate an allowed feed/API/crawler method before selecting it. Official arXiv RSS/Atom documentation https://info.arxiv.org/help/rss.html describes subject feeds and daily updates; its cadence need not be 15 minutes. Review current source terms/rate/access requirements before implementation. HN candidates remain https://news.ycombinator.com/rss and https://github.com/HackerNews/API . No subscriptions, mailbox connections, model calls or paid access in this task.

Near-term pilot task: PPY-3212f123-2cc6-4464-b3b6-1c32bfbdda25. End-to-end recurring/classification behavior: PPY-b8b15cfc-f06e-4f19-9574-00c3c233d56c.

LATEST first milestone and implementation scope: real recurring Monitor -> persisted deduplicated References and provenance -> the correct publication's REAL Cyclotron prediction -> human review in the EXISTING curation UI -> an authorized human label under current authority rules -> verified applied steering/training receipt. Predictions, agent judgments and advisory feedback never count as human labels. Recorded, queued and applied feedback are distinct; claim training/optimization only with an applied receipt, never from prediction alone. Respect existing proof/authorization gates; do not bypass them to manufacture a receipt.

One configured Monitor per initial publication is sufficient. Start with 1–2 source adapters: Hacker News first, then a verified current Hugging Face paper/academic source only as a useful bounded increment. Initial consumers are Anth.us, the academic Papyrus publication and Threat Intelligence; exact source-to-publication mapping is flexible and one upstream source may serve multiple independently scoped classifiers. Verify current application/binding ownership and guidance; never assume legacy dbsyytcm9drqa. Pilobolus is not an initial target because its serendipitous content is harder to monitor, not because it is permanently excluded. Preserve recurring, source-appropriate cadence around 15 minutes, checkpoints, dedup/new/updated items, provenance and visible stage failures so relevant discoveries and the learning loop are available for morning review.

Rich Monitoring UI/new inbox, email/unsubscribe, expensive LLM section/desk triage and Markus for everything are MUCH LOWER priority and MUST NOT block this slice. Use existing capabilities and curation UI; choose the operator/configuration interface during implementation, with no required new configuration UI. Additional adapters, 3–5 source expansion and richer views are later increments. Reuse current scheduling/intake/classification/label paths and coordinate intake PR367 instead of duplicating it.

Ryan explicitly authorized implementation of THIS first slice after filing, with public-source intake/classification needed for it. That does not authorize production merge/deployment, new persistent access/IAM, purchases, mailbox/MX changes, subscriptions, AWS-console browser work or unrelated benchmarks. No fabricated human labels. Other new feature plans remain unstarted.
